judged_text: Existing-attendee and blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out, and if the entire submitted list is filtered the user gets a BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which misreports the actual reason (blacklist or duplicate of current attendee). An organizer adds one already-invited email plus one blacklisted email: both are dropped, the user sees 'emails must be unique and valid' even though the input was unique and valid, and partial additions (some guests silently skipped) happen with no per-guest feedback.

record.issue_text: [BUG] Existing-attendee and blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out, and if the entire submitted list is filtered the user gets a BAD_REQUEST with message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which misreports the actual reason (blacklist or duplicate of current attendee). adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, submitted `guests` are filtered into `uniqueGuests` by removing (a) emails already in `booking.attendees` and (b) emails in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (see `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). If everything is filtered out, the handler throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is misleading when the actual reason is “already an attendee” or “blacklisted”, not invalid/duplicate-within-input. If only some are filtered, the remaining are added via `createMany` and success is returned with no indication that some were skipped (UI always toasts `t("guests_added")`). This matches the finding’s described behavior.
